note: SNUPN variants impacting snRNP nuclear transport were first characterized causing childhood-onset LGMD (LGMDR29), with spectrum later expanding to adult-onset and SCA.

evidence.text: SNUPN variants impair snurportin-1 mediated nuclear transport of snRNPs, presenting with proximal weakness starting in childhood along with respiratory dysfunction and contractures.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures, although inter-individual variability in terms of severity even in individuals from the same family was found.

evidence.text: LGMDR29 encompasses congenital to childhood-onset muscular dystrophy, as well as adult-onset and multi-system phenotypes, associated with at least 12 distinct variants affecting importin-beta binding and snurportin-1 function.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia. So far, 12 different variants have been described.
